hypothesis.title: PD35 — KR Lottery-Preference Penalty Composite (4-Factor) — 5th Orthogonal Alpha Source
hypothesis.description: 한국 시장 retail-heavy 구조 특성 + 글로벌 lottery preference penalty 메커니즘 적용. 4-factor expanding-IC-aligned composite (M22_Max_Return + D43_Skewness + L42_Vol_Skewness + D58_Vol_Asymmetry). 학술 메커니즘: 투자자가 '복권성' 종목 (high MAX return, positive skew, downside vol asymmetry) 에 ex-ante 과지불하여 이러한 종목들이 ex-post underperform → high-lottery-attribute 종목 매도, low-lottery-attribute 종목 매수가 alpha 산출. KR 한정 retail attention bias 강화. PIT-strict expanding 36m IC-aligned direction (no full-sample sign flip, PD32 v3b PIT C13 위반 회피).
hypothesis.expected_role: core_diversifier_5th_orthogonal_source — 1715 H1 (Consensus C01-06 + Defense Q07/M08/Q25) + NEW Vol/Skew (D43+D41+D58) + TSMOM + KR_10y와 직교한 lottery-preference penalty axis. cor_per_date_mean=+0.0368 (PD27 1715 H1 base와 매우 강한 직교, < 0.30 통과 by margin 8x).
hypothesis.why_now: 도훈 mandate 2026-05-12: '풍부한 학술 references + ML + PG2 강화' 정규 리서치 mandate. 본 5th source는 C_softmax raw foundation (SR 1.0081 Method A canonical PIT-CLEAN) + NEW Vol/Skew (PD32 D43+D41+D58, AX-001 v2 PASS reframe) 외 별도 axis. Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw 2011 JFE 99 MAX effect + Boyer-Mitton-Vorkink 2010 RFS 23 ex-ante skewness + Ang-Chen-Xing 2006 RFS 19 downside risk 3중 학술 mechanism.

primary_papers.citation: Bali, T. G., Cakici, N., & Whitelaw, R. F. (2011). 'Maxing out: Stocks as lotteries and the cross-section of expected returns.' Journal of Financial Economics, 99(2), 427-446.
primary_papers.mechanism: Investors over-pay for stocks with high maximum daily returns (MAX) in past month, expecting lottery-like payoffs. High-MAX stocks systematically underperform in subsequent month. Effect strongest among low-priced, high-vol, retail-heavy stocks.
primary_papers.kr_relevance: KR retail trading share 35-50% (vs US 15-25%) → MAX effect amplified. Empirical conditional_value 0.027 (recent 3y ICIR -0.59 reversal, IC-aligned positive direction).

primary_papers.citation: Boyer, B., Mitton, T., & Vorkink, K. (2010). 'Expected idiosyncratic skewness.' Review of Financial Studies, 23(1), 169-202.
primary_papers.mechanism: Forward idiosyncratic skewness estimated from past returns/volume. Investors prefer positive skew → high expected-skew stocks earn lower future returns. Predicts ~7% annual underperformance for top decile skew.
primary_papers.kr_relevance: D43_Skewness factor: 21-day rolling 3rd moment standardized. Direct empirical implementation.

primary_papers.citation: Kumar, A. (2009). 'Who gambles in the stock market?' Journal of Finance, 64(4), 1889-1933.
primary_papers.mechanism: Lottery-stock preference concentrated among retail investors (low income, low education, young, male). Retail participation → mispricing → reversal.
primary_papers.kr_relevance: KR retail composition: 60%+ trade volume from retail (KOFIA 2023). Direct evidence for lottery effect amplification.

primary_papers.citation: Ang, A., Chen, J., & Xing, Y. (2006). 'Downside risk.' Review of Financial Studies, 19(4), 1191-1239.
primary_papers.mechanism: Stocks with high downside beta (covariance with market during down markets) demand return premium. Asymmetric vol → asymmetric loss aversion (Kahneman-Tversky 1979 prospect theory).
primary_papers.kr_relevance: D58_Vol_Asymmetry: 21-day downside vol / upside vol. Direct downside risk metric.

primary_papers.citation: Ang, A., Hodrick, R. J., Xing, Y., & Zhang, X. (2006). 'The cross-section of volatility and expected returns.' Journal of Finance, 61(1), 259-299.
primary_papers.mechanism: Idiosyncratic vol puzzle — high-IVOL stocks earn lower returns (opposite to CAPM). Mechanism: arbitrage limits + lottery-like demand from retail.
primary_papers.kr_relevance: Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan 2015 JF 70 arbitrage asymmetry — KR retail-heavy market amplifies.

primary_papers.citation: Conrad, J., Dittmar, R. F., & Ghysels, E. (2013). 'Ex ante skewness and expected stock returns.' Journal of Finance, 68(1), 85-124.
primary_papers.mechanism: Risk-neutral skewness from options predicts negative cross-sectional return. Confirms Boyer-Mitton-Vorkink 2010 with option-implied data.

primary_papers.citation: Harvey, C. R., Liu, Y., & Zhu, H. (2016). '… and the cross-section of expected returns.' Review of Financial Studies, 29(1), 5-68.
primary_papers.mechanism: Multi-testing inflation in factor research. 316 published factors → effective t-stat threshold 3.0+ (vs naive 2.0).
primary_papers.applied_in_pd35: N_TRIALS=16 (Iter1-5 + PD24 + PD27 + PD32 v2 + PD32 v3b + PD35) → conservative t_HLZ threshold = sqrt(2·log(16)) + 0.55 ≈ 2.90. Observed t_NW=4.97 PASS.

primary_papers.citation: Bailey, D. H., & López de Prado, M. (2014). 'The deflated Sharpe ratio.' Journal of Portfolio Management, 40(5), 94-107.
primary_papers.mechanism: DSR adjusts Sharpe for skewness/kurtosis + multi-testing E[max_SR] under null. PSR z-score conservative significance test.
primary_papers.applied_in_pd35: DSR_z = 3.80 (sigma_sr=0.058, E_max_null=0.104, ICIR_naive=0.325) PASS at any reasonable threshold.

axis_4_ml_consideration_decision_note.decision: PD35 v1 evaluated ML stacking via tree/NN composite over 7 factors (Q10/Q01/Q17/M22/D44/AC22/Q33). Conclusion: ML not applied for THIS WT because:
reasons: Sample N=298 months × ~2400 tickers = 715K observations is large but per-month cross-section ~2400 is small for NN regularization.

Gu-Kelly-Xiu 2020 (RFS 33: 2223-2273) finding: NN/RF gain is primarily from nonlinear FACTOR INTERACTIONS, not new SIGNALS. With 7 factors of known economic mechanism, EW composite captures 90%+ of NN gain in their Table 3.
Chen-Pelger-Zhu 2024 (working paper): deep characteristic-augmented factor model. KR data N too small for separable optimization.
Avramov-Cheng-Metzker 2023 (RFS 36: 6244-6289): ML returns reduce to factor exposures after economic restrictions. PIT/cost/turnover constraint dominates ML alpha source.

TRADE-OFF: ML adds interpretability cost + PIT-strict training cutoff complexity. PD35 prioritizes mechanism-grounded composite. ML as FUTURE EXTENSION reserved for next WT iteration when factor zoo > 30 candidates.
axis_4_ml_consideration_decision_note.ml_alternative_proposed_next_cycle: Next-cycle iteration: LightGBM cross-sectional stacking of TOP-15 conditional_IC factors with monthly expanding training window + SHAP feature attribution + per-month L2 regularization. PIT-strict via training cutoff <= sig_date - 1.

factor_specs.formula: Maximum daily return over rolling 21-day window (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw 2011 MAX implementation)
factor_specs.empirical_sign_kr_via_expanding_IC: Direction inferred per sig_date from expanding IC history (Usable_Date <= sig_date). NO full-sample sign flip (PIT C13 strict).
factor_specs.economic_rationale: Lottery preference penalty — Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw 2011 JFE 99: 427-446. Investors over-pay for high-MAX (lottery) stocks → underperform next 1M. KR retail-heavy amplifies. Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan 2015 arbitrage asymmetry confirms in retail-driven markets.
references: Stambaugh-Yu-Yuan 2015 JF 70: 1903-1948 'Arbitrage Asymmetry and Idiosyncratic Volatility Puzzle'
Kumar 2009 JF 64: 1889-1933 'Who Gambles in the Stock Market?'

factor_specs.formula: Realized idiosyncratic skewness (21-day rolling 3rd moment standardized)
factor_specs.empirical_sign_kr_via_expanding_IC: Direction inferred per sig_date from expanding IC history
factor_specs.economic_rationale: Ex-ante skewness lottery — Boyer-Mitton-Vorkink 2010 RFS 23: 169-202. Investors prefer positive-skew stocks → over-pay → underperform. Conrad-Dittmar-Ghysels 2013 JF 68 option-implied confirmation.
references: Conrad-Dittmar-Ghysels 2013 JF 68: 85-124 'Ex Ante Skewness and Expected Stock Returns'

factor_specs.formula: Volatility distribution skewness (21-day rolling vol distribution asymmetry)
factor_specs.economic_rationale: Vol-skew lottery proxy — Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang 2006 JF 61: 259-299 IVOL puzzle. Positive-vol-skew (occasional vol spikes) acts as lottery proxy.
references: Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang 2006 JF 61: 259-299 'The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns'

factor_specs.formula: Downside / Upside vol asymmetry ratio (21-day rolling separated by negative vs positive returns)
factor_specs.economic_rationale: Downside risk premium — Ang-Chen-Xing 2006 RFS 19: 1191-1239. Stocks with greater downside vol than upside vol demand premium. Kahneman-Tversky 1979 loss aversion theoretical anchor.
